# The miniapp SDK

<!-- Generated by `bun run sdk:render` from src/sdk/contract.ts. Edit the contract, not this file. -->

window.miniapp is the only host surface a Capsule has, in the editor preview and on every Deployment. Each module is a namespace on it. A published call is one or more MCP tool calls to the Deployment's runtime endpoint with the app session cookie.

```js
const session = await miniapp.auth.session();                    // { userId, name, role }; role is "anonymous" when signed out
await miniapp.auth.signIn();                                     // published login page, preview selects Alice
await miniapp.auth.signOut();                                    // revoke this app session
const rows = await miniapp.actions.call("tasks.list");           // array of row objects
await miniapp.actions.call("tasks.create", { title });           // { changes, lastInsertId }
await miniapp.actions.call("lesson.finish", { lesson });         // a signal action: { recorded: true }
const files = await miniapp.files.list();                        // that user's private files, plus public files
const stored = await miniapp.files.upload(file);                 // private to the signed-in user
const shared = await miniapp.files.upload(file, { visibility: "public" });
image.src = await miniapp.files.url(photo.file_id);              // "/_littlebox/files/<id>"
const text = await (await fetch(await miniapp.files.url(note.id))).text();
await miniapp.files.update(draft.id, { visibility: "public" });  // the draft is now published under the same ID
await miniapp.files.delete(note.file_id);                        // { id, deleted: true }
```

There is nothing else: no fetch to other origins, no localStorage contract, no miniapp.db and no SQL from the browser, no miniapp.track and no analytics call: a Signal is declared on a Server Action and recorded when miniapp.actions.call runs it.

Error messages below are the exact text a published app receives as `error.message`. The Editor preview column says where the preview in the editor answers differently.

## Refusals on every call

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Sign in to use Littlebox MCP.` | the Deployment is private and the visitor has no session; actions.call then sends the browser to /_littlebox/login and auth.session returns the anonymous state instead | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Deployment not found.` | the host name matches no Deployment | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Cross-origin or unrecognized-host MCP request rejected.` | the request does not come from the Deployment's own origin | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `MCP request exceeds 200 KB.` | one request body is larger than 200,000 bytes | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Invalid MCP response.` | the response does not answer the request the SDK sent | SDK | Never refuses |

## miniapp.auth

Who is using the app. The Kernel owns accounts and sessions; the app only reads the current one.

- Visibility decides who may open the app shell. It never grants data access on its own.
- The Deployment's Signup Policy, which the owner sets in the editor or with signup_policy_set, decides who may create an account: Open, Invitation only, Closed or an Allowlist. Under Invitation only, the sign-in page offers no account creation; invited people accept from the link in their email, which opens /_littlebox/invitation.

### miniapp.auth.session()

Read the signed-in Runtime Actor, or the anonymous state so the app can show a sign-in button.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: allowed.

Runtime MCP tools: `auth_session`.

Returns { userId, name, role }. Signed in, name is the account email and role is "member" or "owner". Signed out, { userId: "anonymous", name: "Anonymous", role: "anonymous" }.

Editor preview: Returns Alice or Bob, the preview's test accounts, with role "member", or the anonymous state.

### miniapp.auth.signIn()

Send the visitor to the Deployment's login page at /_littlebox/login.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: allowed.

Runtime MCP tools: none.

Returns nothing; the page navigates away.

Editor preview: Signs in as Alice without leaving the page and returns her session.

### miniapp.auth.signOut()

Revoke this app session, clear its cookie and release the file URLs the SDK created.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: refused.

Runtime MCP tools: `auth_logout`.

Returns { ok: true }.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `authentication-required` | no one is signed in | Kernel | Never refuses |

Editor preview: Switches to the signed-out state and returns the anonymous session.

## miniapp.actions

The only door to the database. A call names a Server Action declared in actions.json and passes its input; the Kernel authorizes the caller, binds the input and runs the action's one SQL statement, or records its Signal.

- A query action returns the rows of its SELECT. Column names are exactly the ones the SELECT projects, so alias any expression the app reads.
- A mutation action returns { changes, lastInsertId }. Read changed rows with a separate query.
- The Action Contract, action-contract.json, lists every action with its inputs, the columns it returns, its errors and limits. It is written from actions.json and schema.sql by littlebox contract and carried in the export; an expression the SELECT returns without AS has no name in it, and the Validation Gate warns.
- To record that something happened, such as a signup to a newsletter or a finished lesson, declare a signal on the mutation that does it, or add an action of kind signal and call it with miniapp.actions.call. There is no other tracking call.
- A call the Kernel refuses records no Signal and counts in no Usage total.

Declared with `signal` in `actions.json`. { "name": "order.placed", "properties"?: ["input binding keys"] } on a mutation, or on an action of "kind": "signal" that has access and bindings but no statement. When the action succeeds the Kernel records the Signal with the named inputs as its properties, in the Deployment's Usage store. A signal action runs no SQL and returns { recorded: true }. The owner reads Signals with signals_read; the app cannot. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Action <name> is a query, so it cannot declare a signal. Declare it on a mutation or on a "kind": "signal" action.` | the action is a query | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names signal property <key>, which is not one of its input bindings.` | a property is not the key of an input binding; actor, kernel and literal bindings have no key | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names signal property <key> twice.` | properties lists a key twice | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names more than 8 signal properties.` | properties lists more than 8 keys | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names an invalid signal. Use dot-separated lowercase words, such as "order.placed", up to 64 characters.` | the name has one word, a capital, a space, an empty part or more than 64 characters | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> has an invalid signal declaration.` | signal is not an object, has a key other than name and properties, has no name, or properties is not a list of strings | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> is a signal action, so it must declare a signal.` | the kind is signal and there is no signal key | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> is a signal action, so it runs no SQL and cannot declare a statement.` | the kind is signal and the action has a statement | Kernel | Same |

Limits:

- 8 properties per Signal; a string property keeps its first 128 bytes
- a signal action counts toward the action limit like any other action
- a signal action cannot declare http
- the Kernel keeps the newest 50,000 Signals per Deployment and drops the oldest

### miniapp.actions.call(name, input = {})

Invoke one declared Server Action as the current Runtime Actor.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: allowed.

Runtime MCP tools: `actions_invoke`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | A Server Action name declared in actions.json, e.g. tasks.list |
| `input` | `object` | No | One value per input binding of the action, keyed by the binding's key. Defaults to {} |

Returns an array of row objects for a query action, { changes, lastInsertId } for a mutation action, { recorded: true } for a signal action.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Server action not declared.` | actions.json declares no action with that name | Kernel | `Server action not declared: <name>` |
| `authentication-required` | the action is not declared anonymous and no one is signed in; the published SDK also sends the browser to /_littlebox/login | Kernel | Same |
| `rate-limited` | more than 30 calls in 10 seconds from one signed-out client address on one Deployment, or 120 from one signed-in user | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Arguments must be an object.` | input is not an object, e.g. null | Kernel | `Action input must be an object.` |
| `Expected a string.` | name is not a string | Kernel | `Server action not declared: <name>` |
| `Unexpected action input: <key>` | input has a key no input binding declares | Kernel | Same |
| `This action requires an authenticated actor.` | an anonymous action binds the actor id and no one is signed in | Kernel | Same |
| `Missing action input: <key>` | a required input is omitted | Kernel | `<key> must be a non-empty string.` or `<key> must be a finite number.` or `<key> must be a boolean.` |
| `<key> must be a non-empty string.` | a string input is not a string, or is empty or only whitespace | Kernel | Same |
| `<key> is too long.` | a string input is longer than its maxLength in UTF-16 code units | Kernel | Same |
| `<key> must be a number.` | a number input is not a JSON number | Kernel | `<key> must be a finite number.` |
| `<key> must be a boolean.` | a boolean input is not true or false | Kernel | Same |
| `Query result exceeds 2 MiB or 1000 rows.` | a query produces more than 1000 rows or more than 2 MiB of JSON | Kernel | `Query returned more than 1000 rows. Add a LIMIT clause.` or `Query result is too large.` |

Limits:

- 30 calls per 10 seconds per signed-out client address and Deployment; 120 per 10 seconds per signed-in user
- 1000 rows and 2 MiB per query result
- 2 seconds per statement; SQLite's own error text is returned when a statement fails or runs out of time
- string inputs default to a maxLength of 10,000 UTF-16 code units
- 256 MiB per app database

Editor preview: Ignores the Deployment's visibility and rate limits, and keeps its database in the browser with a 10 MiB cap. A signal action returns { recorded: true } and records nothing; Signals exist only on a Deployment or a Development Kernel.

## miniapp.files

Small files stored by the Kernel for one Deployment. A file is private to the user who uploaded it unless the upload asked for public.

- Only the uploader can list or read a private file.
- On a public Deployment a signed-out visitor can list and read public files. On a private Deployment any signed-in user can.
- files.list and files.upload download over MCP, check the SHA-256 and return a Blob URL. The page's policy allows connect-src 'self' only, so fetch cannot read a Blob URL again. To fetch a file, or to show one without downloading every file, use files.url. It returns the file's path GET /_littlebox/files/<id> on the app's own origin, which img, fetch and a link all reach.
- The uploader alone changes a file's visibility with files.update or deletes it with files.delete. A deleted file stops counting against the 20 MiB quota and its ID answers File not found from then on, through every door.
- A visitor without a session on a private Deployment is asked to sign in before any file is looked up: 401 authentication-required. On a public Deployment, a file the visitor may not read answers 404 File not found, the same as a missing one. A signed-in user who may not read a file also gets 404.

### miniapp.files.list()

List and download every file the current actor may read.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: allowed.

Runtime MCP tools: `files_list`, `files_read`, `transfer_read`, `transfer_cancel`.

Returns an array of { id, name, type, size, visibility, createdAt, ownerId, url }. ownerId is present only on files the caller uploaded. url is a Blob URL; it keeps the type for image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp and image/avif and is application/octet-stream otherwise.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `File not found.` | the file was removed or the actor may not read it | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Too many active transfers. Cancel completed transfers before starting another.` | the actor already holds 2 transfers, or the Deployment holds 32 | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Transfer not found or expired.` | a transfer outlived its 10 minutes | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Invalid file size.` | the Kernel announced a size outside 0 to 2 MiB | SDK | Never refuses |
| `Invalid file block.` | a downloaded block does not continue at the expected offset or exceeds 64 KiB | SDK | Never refuses |
| `File checksum mismatch.` | the downloaded bytes do not match the SHA-256 the Kernel announced | SDK | Never refuses |

Limits:

- every listed file is downloaded, one at a time, on each call
- 2 MiB per file

Editor preview: Reads files from browser storage and returns data URLs.

### miniapp.files.upload(file, options)

Store a File or Blob for the signed-in user and return it as files.list would.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: refused.

Runtime MCP tools: `transfer_begin`, `transfer_write`, `transfer_complete`, `files_upload`, `transfer_cancel`, `files_read`, `transfer_read`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `file` | `File \| Blob` | Yes | The bytes to store, with its name and type |
| `options.visibility` | `"private" \| "public"` | No | "private", the default, keeps the file to the uploader. Pass "public" only when every visitor of a public app may read the bytes. Any other value is refused before the upload starts |

Returns { id, name, type, size, visibility, createdAt, ownerId, url }. ownerId is present only on files the caller uploaded. url is a Blob URL; it keeps the type for image/png, image/jpeg, image/gif, image/webp and image/avif and is application/octet-stream otherwise.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `authentication-required` | no one is signed in | Kernel | Same |
| `File visibility must be private or public.` | visibility is anything other than "private" or "public"; the SDK refuses before it sends anything | SDK | Same |
| `Transfer size is outside the limit.` | the file is empty or larger than 2 MiB | Kernel | `Local prototype files are limited to 2 MiB.` |
| `This deployment has reached its 20 MiB file quota.` | the Deployment's files would exceed 20 MiB together | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `File not found.` | the file was removed or the actor may not read it | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Too many active transfers. Cancel completed transfers before starting another.` | the actor already holds 2 transfers, or the Deployment holds 32 | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Transfer not found or expired.` | a transfer outlived its 10 minutes | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Invalid file size.` | the Kernel announced a size outside 0 to 2 MiB | SDK | Never refuses |
| `Invalid file block.` | a downloaded block does not continue at the expected offset or exceeds 64 KiB | SDK | Never refuses |
| `File checksum mismatch.` | the downloaded bytes do not match the SHA-256 the Kernel announced | SDK | Never refuses |

Limits:

- 1 byte to 2 MiB per file
- 20 MiB of files per Deployment
- 2 transfers at a time per user and 32 per Deployment; each expires after 10 minutes
- the name is cut to 180 characters with / and \ replaced by -; a type of 128 characters or more, or with a character other than a letter, a digit or one of !#$&^_.+-/, becomes application/octet-stream

Editor preview: Stores the file in browser storage as a data URL, and accepts an empty file.

### miniapp.files.url(fileId)

The address of a stored file on the app's own origin, for an img src, a link or a fetch.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: allowed.

Runtime MCP tools: none.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fileId` | `string` | Yes | The id of a file from files.list or files.upload, or one an action returned |

Returns a Promise of the path "/_littlebox/files/<id>". Reading it answers the file's bytes with its own type when the caller may read it, 404 File not found when the file is missing, deleted or not theirs, and 401 authentication-required to a visitor of a private Deployment.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `A file ID is required.` | fileId is not a non-empty string | SDK | Same |
| `File not found.` | reading the path, when the file does not exist, was deleted, or the caller may not read it (404) | Kernel | Same |
| `authentication-required` | reading the path on a private Deployment without a session (401) | Kernel | Never refuses |

Limits:

- the path answers with Cache-Control: private, no-store and Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy: same-origin, so another site cannot embed it
- PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and AVIF answer inline; every other type downloads as an attachment

Editor preview: Returns the file's data URL from browser storage, and refuses at the call with File not found when the preview actor may not read the file.

### miniapp.files.update(fileId, { visibility })

Make a file the signed-in user uploaded public or private. Publishing a draft keeps its ID, so no second copy counts against the quota.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: refused.

Runtime MCP tools: `files_update`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fileId` | `string` | Yes | The id of a file the signed-in user uploaded |
| `visibility` | `"private" \| "public"` | Yes | "public" lets every signed-in user, and every visitor of a public app, read the file; "private" keeps it to the uploader |

Returns { id, name, type, size, visibility, createdAt, ownerId } with the new visibility. There is no url; the ID and its files.url path stay the same.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `authentication-required` | no one is signed in | Kernel | Same |
| `A file ID is required.` | fileId is not a non-empty string | SDK | Same |
| `File visibility must be private or public.` | visibility is anything other than "private" or "public"; the SDK refuses before it sends anything | SDK | Same |
| `File not found.` | the file does not exist, was deleted, or the caller may not read it | Kernel | Same |
| `Only the person who uploaded this file may change or delete it.` | the caller may read the file but did not upload it | Kernel | Same |

### miniapp.files.delete(fileId)

Delete a file the signed-in user uploaded. Its bytes are gone and its size stops counting against the Deployment's quota.

Signed-out visitors on a public Deployment: refused.

Runtime MCP tools: `files_delete`.

| Argument | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fileId` | `string` | Yes | The id of a file the signed-in user uploaded |

Returns { id, deleted: true }.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `authentication-required` | no one is signed in | Kernel | Same |
| `A file ID is required.` | fileId is not a non-empty string | SDK | Same |
| `File not found.` | the file does not exist, was already deleted, or the caller may not read it | Kernel | Same |
| `Only the person who uploaded this file may change or delete it.` | the caller may read the file but did not upload it | Kernel | Same |

Limits:

- a row that still names the file ID keeps it; the app removes that row with its own action

## The http module, declared, with no browser call

Routes on the Deployment's own host for programs and other services: a JSON endpoint, a webhook, a file a program fetches. There is no browser call; the app's own pages keep using miniapp.actions.call, and may use a file's route as an img src.

- Only an action declared anonymous may bind a route, and the route answers whatever the Deployment's visibility. On a private app, a route without a signature is open to anyone who knows the path.
- A route has three kinds of caller: a service that signs the request, a program that sends Authorization: Bearer with an API key the owner issued, and a person signed in to the app, from the app's own origin. An actor binding yields the key's ID or the user's ID; a signed request has no actor.
- A signed route reads the declared header as t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" keyed with the secret>. An API key that names the action replaces the signature.
- The owner sets the secret with the secret_set admin tool before publishing. It never appears in actions.json, the Build Artifact or an export.
- GET /_littlebox/files/<id>, the path miniapp.files.url returns, answers a file the caller may read, with its own type. A person reads by the usual file rules, a visitor reads public files of a public app, and an API key reads the visibilities the owner named on it. A visitor without a session on a private app gets 401 authentication-required before any file is looked up; every other caller who may not read the file gets 404 File not found, the same as for a missing or deleted one.
- The editor preview serves no routes. Run them on a Development Kernel with littlebox dev, or on a Deployment.

Declared with `http` in `actions.json`. { "method": "GET" | "POST", "path": "/api/items", "signature"?: { "header": "X-Signature", "secret": "items_webhook" } } on an action declared anonymous. GET binds a query and maps the query string onto its input bindings by type; POST binds a mutation and reads a JSON object body. The route answers { result } with the rows or { changes, lastInsertId }, and { error } with a status code. The Validation Gate and the Kernel refuse the same declarations with the same messages.

| Message | When | Source | Editor preview |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Action <name> must bind GET for a query and POST for a mutation.` | the method does not match the action's kind, or is neither GET nor POST | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> is authenticated, so it cannot declare http. Only anonymous actions answer on an HTTP route.` | the action's access is authenticated | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> has an invalid http path. Use a leading "/" and segments of letters, digits, ".", "_", "~" or "-", up to 200 characters.` | the path is "/", ends with "/", climbs with "..", or carries a query string | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> binds the reserved path <key>. Paths under /_littlebox, /oauth, /.well-known and /mcp belong to the Kernel.` | the first segment is reserved, in any letter case | Kernel | Same |
| `Actions <name> and <name> both bind <key>.` | two actions declare the same method and path | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> has an invalid signature header.` | the header is not 1 to 64 letters, digits and -, or is Authorization, Cookie, Host, Content-Type or Content-Length | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> names an invalid signature secret. Use lowercase letters, digits and "_", starting with a letter.` | the secret is not a secret name | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> has an invalid http binding.` | http is not an object, has another key, or its signature has a key other than header and secret | Kernel | Same |
| `Action <name> signs with the secret <name>, which is not set for this project. Set it with secret_set before publishing.` | publishing, and the owner has not set the secret; the editor cannot see secrets, so only the Kernel refuses this | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `invalid-signature` | a signed route gets no signature, a wrong one, or a t more than 300 seconds from the Kernel's clock (401) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `replayed-signature` | the same signature arrives a second time (409) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `invalid-api-key` | Authorization carries an lbk_ key that is unknown or revoked (401) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `This API key may not call <name>.` | the key does not name the route's action (403) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `No route accepts POST on this path.` | a POST reaches a path no action binds (405) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `A route does not answer HEAD. Send GET.` | a HEAD reaches a path a query binds; it is refused before any SQL, with Allow: GET (405) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `The request body exceeds 64 KiB.` | a POST body is larger (413) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `The request body must be a JSON object.` | a POST body does not parse as JSON (400) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `Repeated query parameter: <key>` | a GET names one input twice (400) | Kernel | Never refuses |
| `rate-limited` | a caller exceeds the action limits of the runtime endpoint, or its address sent 10 unknown or revoked API keys to the Deployment in a minute (429, with Retry-After) | Kernel | Never refuses |

Limits:

- a POST body of 64 KiB
- a signature's t within 300 seconds of the Kernel's clock, and each signature accepted once
- the runtime endpoint's action rate limits: 30 per 10 seconds per client address without a key or session, 120 per 10 seconds per user or key
- 50 live API keys per Deployment
